chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the day of the greater pilgrimage.
So he said: It is the Day of Sacrifice, and the smaller one is Umrah.

key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْحَجِّ الْأَكْبَرِ: The day of the greater pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the greater and smaller pilgrimage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this chain to establish the precise temporal definition of Hajj, linking it specifically to the Day of Sacrifice rather than the entire season. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the ritual peak of the pilgrimage, while simultaneously defining Umrah as the 'smaller' counterpart, a classification that underpins the legal requirements for their respective performance and validity.
